extracted.intended_audience: chemical patent indexers and patent searchers (Derwent/Chemical indexing users)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and conventions for assigning Derwent/BCE chemical indexing codes to steroidal structures, natural products, polymers, dyes, enzymes, polypeptides and related chemical entities in patent documents; includes coding exceptions, precedence, and search-subheading mappings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Girard Reagent coding
rubrics_metrics.description: Girard Reagent – includes all acyl hydrazones substituted on the acyl moiety by a quaternary ammonium radical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Girard Reagents are not coded as hydrazones and are not split into “exo” terms, except for halogens. Substituents coded here are not coded under NRR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methyl group (T8) coding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: CH3 represents a methyl group. Specific codes (T801-T823 etc.) are assigned by position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use methyl-group codes at positions 10, 13, 20, 22 or 23+ because methyls in these positions are considered integral parts of the steroid nucleus. When a methyl group is coded also code the 2A term “hydrocarbon chain” and the 2B term “lower alkyl (1-7)”. The “exo” CH3 descriptor is not used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethynyl/-C#C- (T9) coding linkage rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The ethynyl code (-C#C-) is assigned with positional subcodes (T900..T923).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When this ethynyl code is used, also code “hydrocarbon chain” (U001-U023) and “alkynyl” (U035).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hydrocarbon chain (U0) definition and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: HC (hydrocarbon) chain – represents a hydrocarbon chain; specific positional codes U000..U023 and type codes (U030..U035) exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methyl groups at positions 10 and 13 are not coded here (see -CH3 descriptor). In pregnanes, the 2-carbon chain attached to position 17 is not coded as a hydrocarbon unless substituted. In cholesterols and other sterols, the HC chain at positions 17, 20 and 22 is not coded. HC chain may include an aralkyl or cyclic hydrocarbon ring attached via an aliphatic carbon chain but the ring carbons are not counted as chain members. The HC-chain descriptor is not used at positions 20, 22 or 23+ except for 20-, 22- or 23+-ethinyl. “Exo”-HC Chain is not coded except when used with the “exo” -C#C- descriptor. 2-B definitions: L. Alkyl (1-7); Hi. Alkyl (8+); =CH2 includes both H and unsubstituted hydrocarbon substituents at =C; Alkenyl if chain contains a double bond other than at attachment point; With Aromatic for aliphatic side chain substituted by aromatic ring; Alkynyl if chain contains a triple bond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carbocyclic ring (U1) coding
rubrics_metrics.description: Hydrocarbon ring descriptors for rings attached to the steroid nucleus with positional codes U101..U123 and subcodes for ring size, attachment type and saturation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hydrocarbon ring includes any hydrocarbon ring (even with non-hydrocarbon substituents) attached to nucleus positions 1-23+. For fused rings, record the positions on the ring to which it is attached. The “exo”-HC ring descriptor is not used. Use subcodes for ring size (3M,4M,5M,6M,7M+), attachment (Spiro, Fused, Independent), and type (Saturated, Unsaturated non-aromatic, Aromatic).

rubrics_metrics.name: -CN (U2) positional coding
rubrics_metrics.description: -CN substituent is coded with positional subcodes U200 (Exo) and U201..U223 (positions 1..23+).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the positional subcode appropriate to where the -CN radical is attached; follow the general exo/position conventions used elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: COOR (U3) = carboxyl radical coding policy
rubrics_metrics.description: COOR represents carboxylic acid radicals and their salts, esters, amides; includes thioesters, thioamides, and halides. COOR is considered as a unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not code -OH, =O, -NH2 portions of COOR separately. Use 2-B terms to define R (R=H, R=salts, R=alkyl, R=N-containing, R=S-, R=O-, R=halogen-containing, R=other, R=oxalyl). C(O)-X (X=hetero) covers amides/halides; C(X)-O (X=hetero) commonly covers thioesters. The exo C-sub descriptor is not used; the radical substituted on the carbon chain is coded as exo. C-sub is not employed at positions 10, 13, 17, 20, 21, 22 and 23+. Examples: CH2NH2 → code 7-C-sub in 2-A and N-containing group in 2-B, plus “exo” N-R-R and primary amine; CH2Cl → code 21-C-sub in 2-A and “halogen group” in 2-B, also code “exo” halo, chlorine, and 3 carbons at 17 if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: C-substituent (-C-R) (U4) coding principle
rubrics_metrics.description: -C-R (C-subs) represents a non-hydrocarbon substituent linked through a carbon atom to the steroid nucleus and not otherwise specified by other 2-A terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If in doubt, prefer coding as C-sub rather than “Miscellaneous.” Substituted cycloalkyls attached to the nucleus are coded as HC-ring, not as C-sub. Substituting groups on such rings are coded as “exo.” Do not use C-sub where a more specific 2-A term exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addition and maleic adduct coding precedence
rubrics_metrics.description: Addition designates addition compounds (bisulfate addition, hydrates, Grignard addition compounds, etc.). Maleic adducts are steroid reaction products with maleic anhydride or ester adducts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also code under 2-A “Miscellaneous” when possible for addition compounds. Maleic adducts take precedence over all other codes and are only coded as maleic adducts except for coding nuclear substituents; no other codes are used for the adduct. CNO, NCO, NCS, SCN are coded and also coded under 2-A “Miscellaneous” when possible. 21-Diazo is coded as such (not as 21-N-R-R or 21-Misc). i-compounds (3,5-cyclo) are not considered fused compounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carbon chain bonded to position 17 (U5) coding notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Codes U500..U572 and related indicate the number of C atoms and special chain types bonded to C(17).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final digits of U5 codes do not necessarily refer to steroid nucleus position numbers. Vitamin D derivatives or intermediates are coded V340. Use specific U5 codes for 0..10+ carbon atoms and for bile acids, isopregnane, etc. Use bis-substituent codes (U580/U581) when a steroidal carbon is attached to two identical groups; do not use for bismethyl substitutions in the side chain (e.g. cholesterol 26/27 methyls), for hydrogens, or for symmetrical spiro rings (ketals). Distinguish bis-at-C(17) vs bis-at-same-C(not 17).

rubrics_metrics.name: General rules for 'Exo' designation
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Ex' designates substituents or pairs of double-bonded carbon atoms not directly connected through C–C linkages to the 1–23+ steroid nucleus carbons (i.e., external substituents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: carboxyl substituent in cholic acid is Ex-coded (23+ COOR). The Exo designation is not coded in certain 2A columns (H, CH3, -C-Sub, HC Ring, Misc, HC Chain), except alkinyl -C#C- which is coded as an “Ex” term and when used HC Chain is also coded. For methyl substitutions at positions 10 and 13: when methyls at 10 and 13 are substituted, code substituents from positions 18 and 19 unless those positions are part of a ring; then code from 10 and 13. Exo-S-R and Exo-COOR are used for substituents not directly connected to the nucleus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Part V codes (natural products; polymers) – applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Part V codes refer to antibiotics, vaccines, vitamins, plant extracts, microorganisms, animal extracts, polymers, enzymes, polypeptides, and other natural products whether structure is known or unknown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part V codes are applicable to compounds specifically mentioned in code definitions and to all derivatives unless stated otherwise. Structure-known natural products are structure-coded in Parts A–M; using Part V codes for known-structure natural products may miss references where patentee did not note natural-product status. Part V codes could be used to narrow a structure-code search. A steroid is only coded in Part V if no structure is disclosed, or if the steroid is in a multicomponent composition with at least one non-steroidal natural product. From 1981 forward, processes producing new natural products of unknown structure are coded in Part N.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part V covers synthetic analogues
rubrics_metrics.description: Most Part V codes cover both the specified natural product and similar synthetic compounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: V161 is assigned to both penicillin and ampicillin (natural and synthetic derivative).

rubrics_metrics.name: Source-of-production supplementary codes for natural products
rubrics_metrics.description: From 1981 forward, codes marked with an * in Part V may be combined with source codes to indicate origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plant source codes: V400, V403, V406; Microbial source codes: V500, V540, V550, V560, V570; Animal source codes: V600, V623, subsets V61:, V63:, V64:. Source codes are assigned only if the source is mentioned or readily determined from references. If a source code is assigned without using a code marked with *, also assign the applicable generic source code (V400, V500, or V600).

rubrics_metrics.name: Searching combination of structure codes and Part V codes (subheading mapping)
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure codes and Part V codes use different subheadings over time; the search strategy must account for subheading history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure codes searched with subheading M0 prior to 1970, and with M2 from 1970 forward. Corresponding Part V codes searched with M0 prior to 1970, with M1 from 1970–1980, and with M2 from 1981 forward. Example search logic (Dialog): Pre-1970: S M0 = A LINK V; 1970–1980: S M2 = A AND M1 = V AND NOT M2 = M903; 1981+: S M2 = (A LINK V LINK M903). Equivalent variants given for Orbit/Questel and STN. Follow mapping exactly when combining structure and Part V codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: V0 negation code purpose and assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: V0 is a Part V negation code added (from 1981 forward) to code subfields whose structural codes refer only to natural products to exclude natural-product-only patent records from structure searches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negating V0 eliminates records containing the desired structure codes that pertain only to natural products. Indexers do NOT assign V0 if: (a) the only Part V codes assigned are from Subset V81:; (b) there is any doubt the structure is a natural product or closely related; (c) the structure is very simple and could be overlooked as a listed natural product (e.g., some phosphonomycins and carotenes); or (d) the code subfield also contains codes for structures that are not natural products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antibiotic code-selection rule (V0/V1/V2 sets)
rubrics_metrics.description: Antibiotics are indexed according to the first letter of their generic name using set V0/V1/V2 codes, with special-case codes for important antibiotic types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: an antibiotic whose generic name begins with K gets V110; some important antibiotics have their own code (neomycin V141). Ampicillin (a penicillin derivative) is assigned V161 (“Penicillin”) rather than V010. Assign V001 to antibiotics with no generic name or those represented by numbers/letters (e.g., “antibiotic 123B”).

rubrics_metrics.name: V299 mixtures rule (antibiotics/vaccines)
rubrics_metrics.description: V299 is the code for mixtures of antibiotics and/or vaccines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to 1981 V299 was assigned only to mixtures of two or more antibiotics that had the same “punch code”; from 1981 forward V299 is assigned to all mixtures of two or more antibiotics and/or vaccines. Antibiotic complexes (e.g., gentamycin complex) are usually treated as a single antibiotic rather than as a mixture.

rubrics_metrics.name: V3 vitamins coding notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Set V3 codes are assigned to compounds with vitamin activity and to compounds whose structure is derived from known vitamins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain compounds are NOT considered vitamins in Set V3 (e.g., nicotinic acid, pantothenic acid, folic acid, choline, inositol, biotin, p-aminobenzoic acid, linoleic acid, and other unsaturated aliphatic acids). Prior to 1981 V399 was used for mixtures of two or more vitamins that shared a punch code; from 1981 V399 is assigned to all mixtures containing two or more vitamins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant-extracts (V4) and alkaloid treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Set V4 covers plant extracts and subsets for various alkaloid classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alkaloids of known structure that cannot be classified in subsets V41:–V46: (e.g., berberine, strychnine) are coded by structure only and NOT in Part V. V402 covers compounds of unknown structure and (from 1981) steroid glycosides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microorganism coding (V5) – scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Each code in Set V5: covers microorganisms and their extracts/metabolites for which they are defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codes cover extracts and metabolites unless these can be more specifically described elsewhere. For example, an antibiotic produced by a microorganism is coded in Set V2: (“Antibiotics and Vaccines”) rather than in Set V5:.

rubrics_metrics.name: V7 polymers and natural polymers coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Set V7: codes cover all natural polymers; polymers involved in pharmaceutical, veterinary, or medical inventions; and all natural products not classifiable elsewhere in Part V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polymeric dyes are coded in Subset W31:. Modifying groups on polymeric materials (e.g., cellulose derivatives) are additionally structure-coded in Parts A–M. For polysaccharides of known vs unknown structure, additional subset codes (e.g. L81, L83, L810) may be applied as noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enzyme and enzyme-inhibitor coding (V8/V80/V81)
rubrics_metrics.description: Set V8/V80/V81 provide codes for enzymes, coenzymes, enzyme inhibitors, and types of enzyme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: V800..V805 designate enzyme/coenzyme/general descriptors. Codes V802, V803, and P616 (Non-polymeric enzyme inhibitor of known structure) are used in combination with subset V81 codes that identify enzyme type. V803 is only used for polymeric or unknown-structure enzyme inhibitors; non-polymeric inhibitors use P616.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polypeptide coding rules (V9) – length and structure handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Set V9 codes cover polypeptides and related descriptors, with subcodes for source, length, and structural type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use V9 codes for dipeptides. Amino acid chains with 1–3 alpha amino acid units are indexed as non-polymeric compounds and structure-coded in Parts D–M. From 1981 forward, a 3-unit chain receives Part V codes in an M2 subfield. Chains of 4+ alpha amino acids are indexed as polypeptides; structure codes for individual amino acids are listed in a single code subfield under subheading M1; amide linkages are NOT coded. Codes in M1/M2/M3 have only been assigned to polypeptides since 1981. Negation codes from Parts H–L may be applied to polypeptides (excluding amide links). The “Basic Group” code for polypeptides is M423.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polypeptide source and synthesis coding (V90)
rubrics_metrics.description: V901 indicates natural origin; V902 indicates synthetic or semisynthetic polypeptides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a patent discloses a synthesis of a polypeptide, code V902 is assigned even if the polypeptide is obtainable from a natural source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part W (dyes) scope and interactions with structure coding
rubrics_metrics.description: Part W codes are assigned to organic compounds used as colouring matter (dyes, pigments, immediate precursors), dyeing processes and treated materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dyes also receive structure codes from Parts A–M and non-structure codes from other Parts. All dye codes are searched with subheading M4. Immediate dye/pigment precursors receive Part W codes plus Q317 (oxidative dye precursor) or Q318 (non-oxidative dye precursor) as applicable. Natural dyes of unknown structure are additionally coded V792 and M423. Fluorescent-coloured compounds get Part W codes and Q613. Indicators, liquid crystals, fluorescent compounds other than brighteners, pearlescent pigments, white pigments, photoconductors, scintillators, etc., are NOT coded in Part W. Conventional non-essential counter ions in ionic dye salts or diazonium compounds are not coded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conventions for selecting dye-form coding (preferred structural forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain dye families and precursors are coded in preferred structural forms rather than their literal form in the disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Keto-hydrazone dyes coded as Azo-phenol; Quinone-diazide precursors coded as Diazonium-phenoxide; Tri-aryl methane dyes coded as Carbonium; Xanthene, oxazine dyes coded as Oxonium; Thiazine dyes as Sulphonium; Phenazine/acridine dyes coded in the form having an ionic charge on ring-N. Phthalein and xanthene dyes are coded in the “ring-open” form, while phthalein/xanthene/spiro-pyran precursors are coded in the “ring-closed” form. Ionic cyanine dyes with two heterocyclic end rings are coded twice (charge on each ring); with one heterocyclic ring assume charge is on that ring. Ionic charge assignment may alter hydrogenation state and affect ring structure coding. Metal-complex dyes are coded into different code subfields based on dye-metal-dye or dye-metal-nondye structural arrangement: (dye1)-metal-(dye2) is coded with (dye1)-metal in one field and metal-(dye2) in another; similarly (dye)-metal-(non-dye) is split.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic dye descriptor rules (W00/W01/W03/W04)
rubrics_metrics.description: General dye codes W001..W005 and related subsets provide generic descriptors and counts of substituents/groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assign W001 to pigments (W334), fluorescent brighteners (Q613), couplers (Q311), dye precursors (Q317/Q318), or dye intermediates (Q316). Assign W002 to dyes containing metals complexed in a chelate ring (not to simple metal salts). W003 is assigned to all other dyes (including simple metal salts). W004 and W005 (Dye residue; Reactive group general) are assigned only when insufficient information exists for detailed structure indexing, or a wide range of dyes is disclosed; in such cases index all specific structures disclosed as well. Use W01 subset to count substituents on anthraquinone ring systems; W03 counts number of sulphonic acid groups present; W04 counts number of diazonium groups present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Azo-dye (W1) typing and incomplete-information handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Azo dyes are categorized by number/configuration of azo linkages and by coupling component types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subset W11 codes: mono-azo (W111), dis-azo types (W112..W115 depending on configuration and information), tris/poly-azo (W116). Definitions: A and A’ are diazo components (amino), M is middle component (amino+coupling), E is end coupling component, D is tetraazo (diamino), Z is a “double” coupling component; notation “( )” indicates diazotised and coupled to. If insufficient information is available to assign a specific dis-azo code (W112–W114), assign W115 (dis-azo other/condensed dis-azo). For exhaustive searches, OR W115 with other W11 codes. Subset W12 categorizes coupling components (amino, phenol, aminophenol, heterocyclic coupling including reactive CH2, other specified coupling including aliphatic reactive CH2).
